# Put studies together 
```{r}
# Sequential joins
combined_results <- gemma_results_r1 %>%
  inner_join(gemma_results_r2, by = c("chr", "ps"), suffix = c("_r1", "_r2")) %>%
  inner_join(gemma_results_r3, by = c("chr", "ps"), suffix = c("_r2", "_r3")) %>%
  inner_join(gemma_results_avg, by = c("chr", "ps"), suffix = c("_r3", "_avg"))

# To check the structure
combined_results <- combined_results %>% dplyr::select(chr,ps,p_wald_r1,p_wald_r2,p_wald_r3,p_wald_avg)
combined_results <- as.data.frame(combined_results)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Reshape data to long format
long_data <- combined_results %>%
  dplyr::select(chr, ps, starts_with("p_wald")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("p_wald"),
    names_to = "replicate",
    values_to = "p_value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    logp = -log10(p_value),
    chr = factor(chr), # Make sure chromosome is a factor
    replicate = factor(replicate, 
                      levels = c("p_wald_r1", "p_wald_r2", "p_wald_r3", "p_wald_avg"),
                      labels = c("R1", "R2", "R3", "Average"))
  )

# Create a color vector for all chromosomes
n_chr <- length(unique(long_data$chr))
chr_colors <- rep(c("#89B9AD", "#85586F"), ceiling(n_chr/2))[1:n_chr]
long_data$chr <- as.factor(long_data$chr)
names(chr_colors) <- levels(long_data$chr)

# Create the plot

# Order a df 
long_data <-long_data[order(long_data$chr, long_data$ps),]

## Calculate a fdr 
n_tests <- nrow(combined_results)  # Number of tests (SNPs)
bonf_threshold <- -log10(0.05/n_tests)  # Bonferroni correction
#combined_results$bh_adjusted <- p.adjust(combined_results$p_wald_r1, method="BH")
# Find BH threshold where adjusted p-value = 0.05
#bh_threshold <- combined_results[combined_results$bh_adjusted<=0.1,]

# Print the thresholds
cat("Bonferroni threshold:", (bonf_threshold), "\n")


ggplot(long_data, aes(x = ps, y = logp, color = chr)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(replicate ~ chr, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = chr_colors) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = bonf_threshold, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(1e-5), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Chromosome",
    y = "-log10(p-value)",
    title = "Manhattan Plots for All Replicates"
  )+scale_x_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(x/1000000),
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 3))


```


## Get a proximity to the gene
```{r}
# Read annotation
annotation_tair10 <- fread("/groups/nordborg/projects/ddm1_resilencing/11_resources/ref_genome/Araport11_GFF3_genes_transposons.current.gff", header=F)
annotation_tair10$V1 <- gsub("Chr","", annotation_tair10$V1)
annotation_tair10 <- annotation_tair10[annotation_tair10$V3=="gene" ,] 
annotation_tair10 <- annotation_tair10 %>% select(V1,V4,V5,V9)
```

```{r}
significance_threshold <- 5.5 ## Needs to be adjusted 
significant_snps <- long_data[(-log10(long_data$p_value)) >significance_threshold, ]
head(significant_snps)
#significant_snps <-significant_snps[significant_snps$chr=="4", ]
```
#Map significant SNPs to the genes 
```{r}
####FIND variants near genes###

max_upstream_distance <- 1  # Adjust as necessary
max_downstream_distance <- 1  # Adjust as necessary
snps_near_genes <- vector("list", length = nrow(significant_snps))
# Loop through each SNP to find if it's inside, upstream, or downstream of any gene
for (i in 1:nrow(significant_snps)) {
  snp <- significant_snps[i, ]
  genes_on_chr <- annotation_tair10[annotation_tair10$V1 == snp$chr, ]
  is_near_or_inside_gene <- (genes_on_chr$V4 - max_upstream_distance <= snp$ps & snp$ps <= genes_on_chr$V5 + max_downstream_distance) |
    (genes_on_chr$V4 <= snp$ps & snp$ps <= genes_on_chr$V5)
  
  if (any(is_near_or_inside_gene)) {
    temp_df <- genes_on_chr[is_near_or_inside_gene, ]
    temp_df$snp_position <- snp$ps
    temp_df$chromosome <- snp$chr 
    temp_df$replicate <- snp$replicate
    temp_df$pval <- -log10(snp$p_value)
    snps_near_genes[[i]] <- temp_df
  } else {
    snps_near_genes[[i]] <- NULL
  }
}

snps_near_genes_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(snps_near_genes, function(df) {
  if (is.null(df)) return(NULL)
  df
}))

```

## Get top genes per replicate
```{r}
# Function to get top 3 genes per chromosome for a specific replicate
get_top_genes <- function(data, rep) {
  # Filter for specific replicate
  rep_data <- data[data$replicate == rep,]
  
  # Group by chromosome and get top 3 genes based on p.value
  top_genes <- rep_data %>%
    group_by(chromosome) %>%
    arrange(pval) %>%
    slice_head(n = 3)
    
  return(top_genes)
}

# Get results for each replicate
R1_top <- get_top_genes(snps_near_genes_df, "R1")
R2_top <- get_top_genes(snps_near_genes_df, "R2")
R3_top <- get_top_genes(snps_near_genes_df, "R3")
R4_top <- get_top_genes(snps_near_genes_df, "Average")

# Print results for each replicate
replicates <- c("R1", "R2", "R3", "Average")
results_list <- list(R1_top, R2_top, R3_top, R4_top)


# Alternatively, combine all results into one dataframe
all_top_genes <- bind_rows(R1_top, R2_top, R3_top, R4_top)
all_top_genes
```

## Combine pvalues 
# Stoffer's method 
```{r}
library(poolr)
p_value_columns1 <- grep("^p_wald", names(gemma_results_r1), value = TRUE)
p_value_columns2 <- grep("^p_wald", names(gemma_results_r2), value = TRUE)
p_value_columns3 <- grep("^p_wald", names(gemma_results_r3), value = TRUE)
p_value_columns4 <- grep("^p_wald", names(gemma_results_avg), value = TRUE)

# Function to combine p-values for each row
combine_p_values <- function(row) {
  # Remove any missing values
  p_values <- na.omit(row)
  # If we have any p-values, combine them
  if(length(p_values) > 0) {
    return(stouffer(p_values)$p)
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
}

gemma_results_r1$combined_p1 <- apply(gemma_results_r1[, ..p_value_columns1], 
                                1, 
                                combine_p_values)
gemma_results_r2$combined_p2 <- apply(gemma_results_r2[, ..p_value_columns2], 
                                1, 
                                combine_p_values)
gemma_results_r3$combined_p3 <- apply(gemma_results_r3[, ..p_value_columns3], 
                                1, 
                                combine_p_values)
gemma_results_avg$combined_p4 <- apply(gemma_results_avg[, ..p_value_columns4], 
                                1, 
                                combine_p_values)
## Select 

gemma_results_r1 <- gemma_results_r1 %>% dplyr::select(chr,ps,combined_p1)
gemma_results_r2 <- gemma_results_r2 %>% dplyr::select(chr,ps,combined_p2)
gemma_results_r3 <- gemma_results_r3 %>% dplyr::select(chr,ps,combined_p3)
gemma_results_r4 <- gemma_results_avg %>% dplyr::select(chr,ps,combined_p4)
```

```{r}
### Optimized Code
# 1. Initial data filtering and conversion
selected_snps <- gemma_results_avg[gemma_results_avg$chr == "5", ] %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("p_wald_"), 
                ~-log10(as.numeric(.)),

# 2. More efficient pivoting with direct -log10 transformation
df_long <- selected_snps %>%
  dplyr::select(ps, chr, starts_with("converted_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("converted_"),
    names_to = "analysis",
    values_to = "p_value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.infinite(p_value), 
         p_value > 3) %>%
  # Remove analyses where all p-values are > 5
  group_by(analysis) %>%
  filter(n() > 0) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. More efficient plotting

median_p <- median(df_long$p_value)
max_p <- max(df_long$p_value)
 # Sort

  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 0.5) +

    colors = c("white", "#FFB4B4", "#CD113B"),

  theme_minimal() +

    axis.title = element_blank(),
```

## Cluster values heriticaly
```{r}
# First, let's prepare the data for clustering
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(dendextend)
library(grid)
library(gridExtra)
library(fastcluster)  

# Assuming df_long has your data
# Create a matrix for clustering


library(fastcluster)  
## Filter to get only the most significant pvalues 
df_long_filtered <- df_long[df_long$p_value>5,]

matrix_for_clustering <- df_long_filtered %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = ps, values_from = p_value) %>%
  column_to_rownames("analysis")
# Fast hierarchical clustering
hc <- fastcluster::hclust(dist(matrix_for_clustering), method = "complete")
dend <- as.dendrogram(hc)

# Get the order of labels after clustering
ordered_labels <- labels(dend)

# Modify your original data with the new ordering
df_long_filtered$analysis <- factor(df_long_filtered$analysis, levels = ordered_labels)

# Create the main plot
ggplot(df_long_filtered, aes(x = ps, y = analysis, color = (p_value))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  scale_color_gradientn(
    colors = c("white", "#FFB4B4", "#CD113B"),
    name = "-log10(P-Value)"
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank())+labs(x = "")
```

### Create a metaGWAS peak 

```{r}
# Load required packages
library(data.table)  # For efficient data handling
library(metap)       # For combining p-values

# Set your input and output folders
input_folder <- "/groups/nordborg/projects/ddm1_resilencing/03_processing/006_gwas/all_plates_96w/limma_gwas/each_te_log2_difference/output/test/"
output_folder <- input_folder

# Step 1: Get list of all files we want to analyze
# Find all files ending with "repl2.assoc.txt"
files_to_read <- list.files(input_folder, 
                           pattern = "*.repl1.assoc.txt", 
                           full.names = TRUE)

# Step 2: Read and process each file
print("Reading files...")
all_data <- list()  # Create empty list to store our data

# Loop through each file
for(i in 1:length(files_to_read)) {
  # Read the file
  current_data <- fread(files_to_read[i])
  
  # Get the TE name from filename (remove "_replX.assoc.txt" part)
  filename <- basename(files_to_read[i])  # Get just the filename
  te_name <- gsub("_repl[0-9]+\\.assoc\\.txt$", "", filename)
  
  # Keep only needed columns and rename p-value column
  current_data <- current_data[, .(chr, ps, p_wald)]
  setnames(current_data, "p_wald", paste0("p_wald_", te_name))
  
  # Store in our list
  all_data[[i]] <- current_data
  
  # Print progress
  print(paste("Processed file", i, "of", length(files_to_read)))
}

# Step 3: Combine all data files
print("Combining all data...")
# Start with the first dataset
combined_data <- all_data[[1]]

# Add each additional dataset
for(i in 2:length(all_data)) {
  combined_data <- merge(combined_data, 
                        all_data[[i]], 
                        by = c("chr", "ps"), 
                        all = TRUE)
  print(paste("Combined dataset", i))
}

# Step 4: Calculate combined p-values
print("Calculating combined p-values...")

# Find all p-value columns (they start with "p_wald")
p_value_columns <- grep("^p_wald", names(combined_data), value = TRUE)

# Function to combine p-values for each row
combine_p_values <- function(row) {
  # Remove any missing values
  p_values <- na.omit(row)
  
  # If we have any p-values, combine them
  if(length(p_values) > 0) {
    return(fisher(p_values, method = "fisher")$p)
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
}

# Add column for number of tests per position
combined_data$n_tests <- apply(combined_data[, ..p_value_columns], 
                             1, 
                             function(x) sum(!is.na(x)))

# Calculate combined p-value for each position
combined_data$combined_p <- apply(combined_data[, ..p_value_columns], 
                                1, 
                                combine_p_values)

# Calculate FDR (adjusted p-values)
combined_data$fdr <- p.adjust(combined_data$combined_p, method = "BH")

# Step 5: Prepare final results
# Keep only the columns we want and sort by chromosome and position
final_results <- combined_data[, .(chr, ps, combined_p, fdr, n_tests)]
final_results <- final_results[order(chr, ps)]

# Step 6: Save results
output_file <- paste0(output_folder, 
                     "combined_TE_pvalues_with_FDR_repl2_", 
                     format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d"), 
                     ".txt")
fwrite(final_results, output_file)

# Step 7: Print summary of results
print("Summary of Results:")
print(paste("Total positions analyzed:", nrow(final_results)))
print(paste("Significant results (FDR < 0.05):", 
           sum(final_results$fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)))
print(paste("Significant results (FDR < 0.01):", 
           sum(final_results$fdr < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

```{r}
# Read files and extract TE names
assoc_files <- list.files("/groups/nordborg/projects/ddm1_resilencing/03_processing/006_gwas/all_plates_96w/limma_gwas/each_te_log2_difference/output/", 
                         pattern = "*.repl2.assoc.txt", 
                         full.names = TRUE)

# Read files into a list of data.tables with TE names as column identifiers
assoc_list <- pblapply(seq_along(assoc_files), function(i) {
  dt <- fread(assoc_files[i])
  # Extract TE name from filename
  te_name <- sub("_repl[0-9]+\\.assoc\\.txt$", "", basename(assoc_files[i]))
  # Rename p_wald column with TE name
  setnames(dt, "p_wald", paste0("p_wald_", te_name))
  dt <- dt[, .(chr, ps, get(paste0("p_wald_", te_name)))]
  return(dt)
})

assoc_list <- pblapply(seq_along(assoc_files), function(i) {
  dt <- assoc_list[[i]]  # Use existing data
  te_name <- sub("_repl[0-9]+\\.assoc\\.txt$", "", basename(assoc_files[i]))
  new_col <- paste0("p_wald_", te_name)
  # Rename the V3 column to proper name
  setnames(dt, "V3", new_col)
  return(dt)
})

# Merge assoc tables 
for (i in seq_along(assoc_list)) {
  setkey(assoc_list[[i]], chr, ps)
}

# Start with first data.table
library(progress)

# Create progress bar
pb <- progress_bar$new(
  format = "Merging [:bar] :percent eta: :eta",
  total = length(assoc_list) - 1,
  clear = FALSE,
  width = 60
)

# Start with first data.table
merged_assoc <- assoc_list[[1]]

# Perform sequential joins with progress bar
for (i in 2:length(assoc_list)) {
  merged_assoc <- merge.data.table(merged_assoc, 
                                  assoc_list[[i]], 
                                  all = TRUE)
  pb$tick()
}
# Extract p-value columns
pval_cols <- grep("^p_wald", names(merged_assoc), value = TRUE)

# Apply Fisher's method to combine p-values for each position
merged_assoc[, combined_p := apply(.SD, 1, function(p) {
  p <- na.omit(p)  # Remove NA values
  if (length(p) > 0) {
    fisher(p, method = "fisher")$p  # Combine using Fisher's method
  } else {
    NA  # Return NA if no valid p-values
  }
}), .SDcols = pval_cols]

# Calculate FDR
merged_assoc[, fdr := p.adjust(combined_p, method = "BH")]

# Select relevant columns and sort by chromosome and position
final_result <- merged_assoc[order(chr, ps), .(chr, ps, combined_p, fdr)]

# Add informative column names to track number of tests combined
n_tests <- merged_assoc[, apply(.SD, 1, function(x) sum(!is.na(x))), .SDcols = pval_cols]
final_result[, n_tests := n_tests]



output_dir <- "/groups/nordborg/projects/ddm1_resilencing/03_processing/006_gwas/all_plates_96w/limma_gwas/each_te_log2_difference/output/"
# Save the result to a file with timestamp

output_file <- file.path(output_dir, paste0("combined_TE_pvalues_with_FDR_repl2", format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d"), ".txt"))

# Write the file
fwrite(final_result, output_file)
# Print summary of significant results at different thresholds
cat("Number of significant results:\n")
cat("FDR < 0.05:", sum(final_result$fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("FDR < 0.01:", sum(final_result$fdr < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
```

```{r}
####FIND variants near genes###

max_upstream_distance <- 500  # Adjust as necessary
max_downstream_distance <- 500  # Adjust as necessary
snps_near_genes <- vector("list", length = nrow(significant_snps))
# Loop through each SNP to find if it's inside, upstream, or downstream of any gene
for (i in 1:nrow(significant_snps)) {
  snp <- significant_snps[i, ]
  genes_on_chr <- mapped_genes[mapped_genes$chromosome_name == snp$chr, ]
  is_near_or_inside_gene <- (genes_on_chr$start_position - max_upstream_distance <= snp$ps & snp$ps <= genes_on_chr$end_position + max_downstream_distance) |
    (genes_on_chr$start_position <= snp$ps & snp$ps <= genes_on_chr$end_position)
  
  if (any(is_near_or_inside_gene)) {
    temp_df <- genes_on_chr[is_near_or_inside_gene, ]
    temp_df$snp_position <- snp$ps
    temp_df$chromosome <- snp$chr 
    temp_df$pval <- snp$p_wald 
    snps_near_genes[[i]] <- temp_df
  } else {
    snps_near_genes[[i]] <- NULL
  }
}

snps_near_genes_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(snps_near_genes, function(df) {
  if (is.null(df)) return(NULL)
  df
}))
```
